title: What is an accountable person?
description: An accountable person is a senior executive individually answerable for part of a regulated firm. How FAR and other senior manager regimes use the term.
shortAnswer: An accountable person is a senior executive whom a regulatory accountability regime makes individually answerable for a defined part of a regulated firm's business or functions, with personal obligations to act with honesty and integrity, with due skill, care and diligence, and to take reasonable steps to prevent breaches. Australia's Financial Accountability Regime uses the term formally; similar senior manager regimes in other markets assign named responsibilities to individuals in comparable ways.
keyTakeaways: An accountable person is defined by actual or effective senior executive responsibility for an area, not by job title.
Under Australia's Financial Accountability Regime (FAR), accountable persons must be registered and named in an accountability map before or soon after taking the role.
The core duty is to take reasonable steps, which FAR describes as including governance, controls, risk management and procedures to identify and fix problems.

Senior manager regimes elsewhere, such as the UK Senior Managers and Certification Regime and the accountable executive under US aviation safety rules, follow the same principle of named individual responsibility.
Training and capability evidence is part of how an accountable person shows they took reasonable steps.

sections.heading: How does the Financial Accountability Regime define an accountable person?

blocks.text: Under Australia's [Financial Accountability Regime Act 2023](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2023A00067/latest/text), section 10(1), an accountable person is someone with actual or effective senior executive responsibility for management or control of an accountable entity or a significant or substantial part of its operations, or who holds a position or responsibility prescribed by the Minister Rules. The regime is jointly administered by the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) and the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC).

FAR replaced the Banking Executive Accountability Regime. It [commenced](https://www.apra.gov.au/cross-industry/financial-accountability-regime-far) for authorized deposit-taking institutions from 15 March 2024 and for insurers and superannuation trustees from 15 March 2025. The [Minister Rules](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2024L00283/latest/text) prescribe responsibilities that must each be held by an accountable person, including risk, compliance, internal audit, the human resource function, breach reporting and the anti-money laundering function.

sections.heading: What must an accountable person do?

blocks.text: An accountable person must meet personal accountability obligations and take reasonable steps to prevent problems in the areas they are responsible for. Section 21 of the FAR Act sets the obligations: act with honesty and integrity, and with due skill, care and diligence; deal with the Regulator in an open, constructive and cooperative way; and take reasonable steps to prevent matters arising that would adversely affect the entity's prudential standing or prudential reputation, or result in a material contravention of listed laws.

Section 22 says reasonable steps include appropriate governance, control and risk management, safeguards against inappropriate delegations of responsibility, procedures for identifying and remediating problems, and appropriate action in response to noncompliance. For a training team, that means the accountable person for a function needs evidence that staff in that function are competent for the obligations they carry. More detail is on [Financial Accountability Regime training](/regulations/financial-accountability-regime-training).

sections.heading: Do other markets have accountable person regimes?

blocks.text: Yes. The label varies, but many regimes require a named individual to hold ultimate responsibility for a defined area. The table compares three examples.

In EU anti-money laundering law, Article 11 of the [Anti-Money Laundering Regulation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1624/oj/eng) requires a compliance manager who is a member of the management body, a narrower version of the same idea; see [money laundering reporting officer](/glossary/money-laundering-reporting-officer).

sections.heading: How is an accountable person different from a responsible manager or a fit and proper person?

blocks.text: An accountable person carries personal accountability for an area; a [responsible manager](/glossary/responsible-manager) under an Australian financial services license supplies the licensee's organizational competence; and [fit and proper](/glossary/fit-and-proper) is a test applied to people in key roles. One individual can be all three. ASIC has said that from 16 October 2026 responsible managers who are also FAR accountable persons face reduced requirements to submit evidence of competence through its Regulatory Portal, with an updated guide expected in the first quarter of 2027.

sections.heading: What does capability evidence for an accountable person look like?

blocks.title: Illustrative example
blocks.text: An insurer's Chief Risk Officer holds the prescribed risk management responsibility. The evidence file shows the accountability statement; a mapping of the obligations in that area to the roles that carry them; competency requirements and assessment results for those roles; completion and assessment data reported to the officer quarterly; and actions taken when a gap was found. The officer's own development record covers changes to the prudential standards in their area.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each obligation in an accountable person's area to the competencies, learning outcomes and assessments of the roles that carry it. That gives the accountable person a traceable view from their accountability statement down to evidence of competence, which supports a reasonable steps record.

faqs.q: Does an accountable person need specific qualifications?
faqs.a: FAR does not set qualifications. Entities must be satisfied the person is suitable, and registration with APRA includes a suitability declaration. Prudential fit and proper requirements and the obligation to act with due skill, care and diligence mean the person must be competent for the area they hold.

Yes. Section 21(2) of the FAR Act allows responsibilities to be shared, but each accountable person sharing a responsibility remains subject to the obligations for it. Clear accountability maps help avoid gaps and unclear overlaps.

faqs.q: What happens if an accountable person fails to take reasonable steps?
faqs.a: Under FAR, consequences can include disqualification, and entities must defer at least 40% of an accountable person's variable remuneration for a minimum of four years and reduce it where obligations are breached. The entity itself faces civil penalties for failing its own obligations.

faqs.q: Is an accountable executive the same as an accountable person?
faqs.a: They are similar ideas in different sectors. The accountable executive under 14 CFR 5.25 is the single person with final authority and ultimate responsibility for an aviation organization's safety performance. FAR accountable persons are usually several executives, each responsible for a defined area.
